 Scoot Henderson (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Henderson has come off the bench in each of Portland’s first two games, most recently playing 21 minutes in Friday’s win over the Kings. If he can’t play on Tuesday, Vit Krejčí may get more playing time, as he played just three minutes against Sacramento. 
 Scoot Henderson 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #00 
 Scoot Henderson accounted for 15 points (7-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Suns. 
 Among the four guards in Portland’s rotation, Henderson (19 minutes) played the least on Wednesday. He played nine of those minutes after halftime, while starters Ja Morant and Damian Lillard and reserve Jrue Holiday (8/4/1/2) logged between seven and nine minutes each. While Henderson having a role won’t be an issue for him, his playing time might be, especially against tougher opponents. 
 Scoot Henderson 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #00 
 Scoot Henderson tallied 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), three assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Monday’s exhibition against the London Lions. 
 With Ja Morant and Damian Lillard added to the roster, Henderson will remain in a reserve role this season. That makes it imperative that he improves his efficiency to provide reliable fantasy value. Over his career, Henderson is a 40.4 percent shooter from the field and has averaged 2.9 turnovers per game. Given Portland’s perimeter depth, Scoot’s fantasy outlook isn’t great, even though he will remain in the rotation. 
 Scoot Henderson 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #00 
 Scoot Henderson finished with five points (2-of-6 FGs), two rebounds and one three-pointer against the Spurs on Tuesday. 
 Henderson’s first playoff appearance had some good moments but ended on a sour note. Through the first three games, he averaged 23.3 points and 4.0 triples, which had many people thinking he was finally showing some of the potential that made him the No. 3 pick in 2023. However, he was held scoreless in Game 4, and while he was able to get some points on the board in this one, he was benched for the end of the game and limited to 17 minutes. Henderson is still only 22 years old and has plenty of time to figure things out, but he’s going to have to make a major leap heading into next season to convince the Blazers he’s still an important part of their future. 
 Jerami Grant 
 POR 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Jerami Grant finished Sunday’s Game 4 loss to the Spurs with 17 points (6-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one block and one three-pointer. 
 After totaling 23 points in the first three games of this series, Grant had his most productive outing in Game 4. Shooting 50 percent from the field, the veteran forward recorded a complete stat line in 33 minutes. With Scoot Henderson (two assists and one steal) missing all seven of his shot attempts, Grant’s playing time jumped considerably, but it wasn’t enough to keep the Trail Blazers from being outscored 73-35 in the second half. Game 5 is on Tuesday, with the Trail Blazers one loss away from elimination. 
 Scoot Henderson 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #00 
 Scoot Henderson had 31 points (11-of-17 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), one rebound, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in the Trail Blazers’ 106-103 Game 2 victory over the Spurs on Tuesday. 
 Henderson found his rhythm with a 15-point second half in Sunday’s Game 1 loss to the Spurs and it carried over to Game 2 as he posted 31 points in the win. The 22-year-old guard’s three-point shooting was a major factor in this one as he was 5-of-9 from behind the arc. The series shifts to Portland for Game 3 on Friday.

 #00 
 Scoot Henderson logged 18 points (7-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in the loss to the Spurs on Sunday. 
 After a quiet, three-point first half, Henderson found his rhythm in his playoff debut and scored 15 points after halftime to finish as Portland’s second-leading scorer on the evening. Henderson shot efficiently in his 27 minutes both inside and outside the arc, and was one of the Blazers’ more reliable starters overall. The former third-overall pick has logged some impressive scoring performances recently in his return from injury. He’ll have a chance to build off some Game 1 momentum and carry it over on Tuesday when the Blazers and Spurs take the floor again.

 Jerami Grant (calf) is out for Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Grant will miss a sixth straight game as he continues to recover from a strained calf. Scoot Henderson has moved into the starting lineup, which has raised his ceiling in active fantasy leagues.

 Scoot Henderson amassed 20 points (7-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, three steals, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 Henderson has scored in double figures in five straight and nine of his last ten appearances. However, he has shot just 40.6 percent from the field during this stretch. That, especially the three-point shooting, is an area where Henderson will need to make strides ahead of the 2026-27 season. And with Damian Lillard (Achilles) re-entering the fray, getting the opportunities needed to affect fantasy basketball will become more challenging for Henderson.

 Jerami Grant (calf) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Clippers. 
 The Trail Blazers still have not revealed a return timeline for Grant, but he will miss a second consecutive game on Tuesday. Scoot Henderson moved into the starting lineup for Sunday’s win over the Wizards and played well, finishing with 21 points and seven assists. Fantasy managers and the Trail Blazers will hope for similar output on Tuesday.

 Cade Cunningham amassed 19 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, eight assists, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks.
 Given Cunningham’s scoring trend in Detroit’s first four games, he’s likely to score 20+ against the Hornets on Wednesday. The Knicks kept him in check for most of the night, with Cade totaling 10 points in the final three quarters of Tuesday’s defeat. The good news for fantasy managers was that he put up quality rebound and assist numbers, finishing one board and two helpers shy of a triple-double.

 Paul Reed tallied 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks.
 Making a second consecutive start for the injured Jalen Duren (hamstring), Reed was hot to start Tuesday’s game. Shooting 5-of-6 from the field, he was responsible for 13 points, three rebounds, three assists, one steal and one blocked shot in the first quarter. Unfortunately for Reed and the Pistons, he went quiet in the second and third quarters, totaling one less foul (four) than points (five) in those periods. As long as Duren’s out, Reed is a must-roster player in fantasy leagues.

 OG Anunoby produced 13 points (5-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons.
 The scoring output was limited, but Anunoby’s complete stat line should benefit category-league managers. Over four games, he’s shooting 38.8 percent from the field, which has hurt OG’s fantasy value. But he’s close to being a top-100 player, and Anunoby provided top-50 fantasy value in each of his first two full seasons in New York. He’ll be fine.

 Karl-Anthony Towns accumulated 27 points (12-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 20 rebounds, three assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons.
 Towns’ only negative on Tuesday was his seven turnovers. He had a good night scoring-wise, and the Knicks’ center finished with his 17th 20/20 game, five of which have occurred since he was traded to New York. Towns was at his best in the third quarter, shooting 5-of-5 from the field and scoring 13 points. He’ll look to build on this showing when the Knicks visit the Bulls on Wednesday.

 Mikal Bridges notched 12 points (4-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons.
 While we aren’t going to proclaim Bridges “back” after a rough first week, Tuesday’s performance was much needed. He shot 4-of-8 from three against the Pistons, including 2-of-4 in the second quarter. New York outscored Detroit 26-12 in the period, rebounding from a slow start. Bridges can be a valuable fantasy option, but many managers were getting close to the point where they had to seriously consider cutting bait. Tuesday’s performance may buy him a little more time. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Brunson recorded 23 points (5-of-18 FGs, 13-of-16 FTs), one rebound and seven assists in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons.
 Ausar Thompson hounded Brunson for most of the night, which contributed to the low field-goal percentage. A busy night at the foul line boosted the point total, and the Knicks guard dished out seven assists, so Brunson gave fantasy managers some value on Tuesday. He’ll look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Bulls.

 Mikel Brown Jr. amassed 17 points (5-of-17 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Active after sitting out Sunday’s loss to the Pacers for injury management reasons, Brown played 28 minutes in Tuesday’s overtime defeat. With Egor Dëmin (leg) leaving in the second quarter and Nolan Traoré (cramps) in the fourth, Brown gained valuable crunch-time experience. His three-pointer with two-tenths of a second remaining forced overtime, but Brown also missed a couple of close-range shots in the extra period that proved costly. Overall, this was an encouraging night for the rookie, even with the outcome and the low field-goal percentage. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Nolan Traoré (cramps) finished Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics with 15 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), one rebound, three assists, two steals and one three-pointer.
 Traoré got off to a good start on Tuesday, scoring 10 points in the first half. Unfortunately, he was relatively quiet after halftime and left the game in the fourth quarter with cramps. Over his last two games, Traoré has totaled 32 points, eight assists, three steals and two blocks. He was inserted into the starting lineup on Tuesday, and the results were encouraging. Traoré isn’t a must-roster player, but he’s worth adding to watch lists in deep leagues.

 Michael Porter Jr. tallied 27 points (8-of-16 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Porter shot 6-of-12 from three on Tuesday, bouncing back from a 0-of-5 effort in Sunday’s loss to the Pacers. He’s made at least four three-pointers in three of Brooklyn’s first four games, and that output is one reason MPJ has been close to a top-25 player through the season’s first week. Another challenging matchup looms, however, as the Nets host the Pistons on Friday.
